# jsPDF 4.2.1: Arabic search compatibility patch

The bundled MIT-licensed jsPDF has two narrowly scoped changes in its UTF-8/font CMap module; all rendering/security APIs remain the pinned upstream version.

1. `pdfEscape16`: for each glyph, store the Unicode NFKC-normalized character rather than the Arabic presentation-form codepoint generated by the shaping step. Multi-character Arabic ligatures are stored in visual glyph order so PDF readers reconstruct logical RTL text correctly.
2. `toUnicodeCmap`: accept a string value and emit its full UTF-16BE sequence, not only a single four-digit codepoint. This retains lam-alef ligatures as searchable standard Unicode without changing the glyph outlines or appearance.

No rasterized/invisible OCR text layer is added. Text is drawn with PDF text operators and embedded Amiri fonts. Tests verify real CMaps, lam-alef mapping, fixed A4 media boxes and unchanged archive input. Browser-generated samples were additionally checked with MuPDF and PDF.js text extraction for the school name, receipt ID and amount in words.

Upstream package: https://registry.npmjs.org/jspdf/-/jspdf-4.2.1.tgz
The original MIT notice remains in `jspdf.umd.min.js` and `JSPDF-LICENSE.txt`. Runtime hashes are recorded in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
